The Solar Position Algorithm (SPA) is a high-precision model developed by NLR to calculate the sun's apparent position from the date, time, and observer location. It uses detailed astronomical models that account for Earth-orbit variations, nutation, aberration, and atmospheric refraction. SPA is widely used in CSP, photovoltaic, solar-resource, and tracking-system applications where high pointing accuracy is required (approximately ±0.0003°). Its primary advantages are sub-arcminute accuracy and broad industry acceptance, while its disadvantages include greater computational complexity and execution cost than simpler engineering formulations such as Duffie & Beckman or SOLPOS.

References: [NLR SPA resources](https://midcdmz.nlr.gov/spa/) and I. Reda and A. Andreas, “Solar Position Algorithm for Solar Radiation Applications (Revised),” NREL/TP-560-34302, January 2008, [doi:10.2172/15003974](https://doi.org/10.2172/15003974).
